# TextWiz — full site context for AI systems

> TextWiz is a native macOS productivity application that runs AI writing shortcuts on text you select. Capture via clipboard (⌘C) + global hotkey (⌘⇧Space) or macOS Services (right-click → Process with TextWiz). No Accessibility APIs. Ten AI engines plus Demo and custom providers; API keys in macOS Keychain; history and analytics in local SQLite. Site: https://textwiz.pro — App source: https://github.com/luongnv89/textwiz

## Product summary

TextWiz ships 14 built-in wizards: 13 visible actions in Everyday Edits (Proofread, Rewrite, Concise, Friendly, Professional), Social (X Post, LinkedIn Post), and Analyst & Coach (Clarity Critic, Executive Summary, Decision Extractor, Rewrite Coach, Argument Stress Test, Structure Tightener), plus Improve Prompt in the wizard editor. Add unlimited custom wizards from Dashboard → Wizards. A floating panel streams responses with an inline diff. Click Copy to close the panel and return focus to your previous app, then paste with ⌘V. If opened from TextWiz itself, Copy just closes it. Auto-copy is optional and off by default; this Copy flow shipped in 1.5.0 build 18.

**Providers:** On-device — Apple Intelligence (Apple Foundation Model, no API key on supported Macs, requires TextWiz Pro), Ollama, LM Studio, MLX-LM. Cloud — Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter. Every real provider requires TextWiz Pro except the Demo provider. One Primary Provider and one Model in Settings apply to all shortcuts.

**Requirements:** macOS 15.2 or later; Apple Intelligence also requires supported hardware. The app is distributed through the Mac App Store, but the latest GitHub release below is not yet available there.

## Draft update — 1.6.0 (build 20)

Build 20 is a draft App Store update and is not yet released. The published GitHub download remains build 19.

- Provider cards start collapsed; Show Settings opens each service independently while names stay visible.
- Official setup and API-key guides appear under each provider card, with clear local and on-device guidance and original provider artwork.
- Add Custom Provider explains the HTTPS API Address, optional API key, and exact Model IDs. Optional headers are under Advanced Settings.
- Missing settings and malformed headers show corrections. Failed saves keep entered settings available for retry. Custom connection checks read the model list; run a wizard to check text generation.

## Latest release — 1.6.0 (build 19), 2026-10-09

TextWiz 1.6.0 (build 19) is [available on GitHub](https://github.com/luongnv89/textwiz/releases/tag/v1.6.0). The Mac App Store update is not yet available.

- Cloud model pickers offer three suggested defaults per provider plus user-added API model IDs. Older catalog models remain available to saved wizards and can be added explicitly.
- Validate & Add checks the specific API model ID before saving for every built-in cloud provider, including Claude, without generating text. A valid key alone does not validate a model.
- Current Claude and GPT-6 requests use supported parameters. Newer Claude and Mythos models omit unsupported sampling parameters; GPT-6 requests to OpenAI omit temperature and use the current output token-limit parameter.
- Claude streamed API errors fail the run with safe recovery guidance. Connection tests distinguish account, network, unexpected-response, and cancellation outcomes.
- macOS Services leaves selected text intact after streamed failure, refusal, or token-limited results and hands off to the floating panel.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible providers require an absolute HTTPS URL with a host and no embedded credentials, query, or fragment. Existing custom HTTP endpoints need HTTPS before use. Built-in local engines keep their HTTP setup.
- Completion and connection failures omit external error bodies and secret-bearing network details. API credentials remain in macOS Keychain.

**Pricing:** the app is a free download. The built-in Demo provider is free and ungated forever. Every run against a real provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Apple Intelligence, LM Studio, MLX-LM, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter) requires TextWiz Pro, an auto-renewable subscription sold through the Mac App Store only. US reference prices: $2.99 per week, $7.99 per month, $59.99 per year. For eligible customers, the weekly plan has an introductory offer of $0.99 charged up front for one week; it then renews at $2.99 per week. Eligibility and the exact price are shown in the App Store before purchase. Monthly and yearly have no introductory offer. Prices are US dollars and vary by region because Apple equalizes them per storefront. Payment is charged to the Apple Account at confirmation of purchase; the subscription renews automatically unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period, with the renewal charge taken within 24 hours before the period ends. Cancel in System Settings > Apple Account > Media & Purchases > Subscriptions. Customers who bought the paid app before the switch to free keep TextWiz Pro for life at no cost.

## How to use TextWiz

1. Copy selected text with ⌘C, press ⌘⇧Space — panel opens with clipboard as input, pick a wizard, then click Copy and paste with ⌘V.
2. Or right-click selection → Services → Process with TextWiz — macOS replaces text after a successful, complete result; failures, refusals, and incomplete results preserve the selection and open the panel.
3. No Accessibility permission; works in sandboxed apps (Slack, VS Code, browsers).

## Setup (getting started)

**Free models and API tokens:** Compare free LLM models and providers at [free-llm-models.custats.info](https://free-llm-models.custats.info/), and find free tokens, trial credits, and API offers at [freetokens.custats.info](https://freetokens.custats.info/). Choose an offer with API access for a TextWiz-supported provider or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, sign up with the provider, create an API key, and follow the setup below. Check the provider's current limits and eligibility before claiming an offer.

**Ollama (local):** `brew install ollama` → `ollama serve` → `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` (or similar) → TextWiz Dashboard → Settings → Primary Provider Ollama → verify server URL → Refresh models → Test Connection → ⌘C + ⌘⇧Space.

**Gemini (cloud):** API key from Google AI Studio → Settings → Primary Provider Gemini → Configure API Key → Save to Keychain → pick model → Test Connection.

Other providers follow the same Settings pattern (API key or server URL for local engines).

**Custom cloud models:** Dashboard → Providers → enter the exact API model ID (including any namespace, such as `author/model` for OpenRouter) → Validate & Add. The model is checked before saving without generating text. Local engines list discovered installed models.

**Custom providers:** Dashboard → Providers → Add Custom Provider → HTTPS base URL including the API prefix, such as `https://api.example.com/v1` → model API IDs one per line. Use the API Key field for credentials, which stores them in macOS Keychain. Additional headers are plaintext routing metadata and should not contain secrets.

## Privacy

- On-device providers: text never leaves the Mac.
- Cloud: only processed text goes to the chosen provider.
- Keys: macOS Keychain only.
- History/analytics: local SQLite, not uploaded.
- Website: static marketing pages; no email signup or on-site feedback forms.
- Payments: Apple processes the TextWiz Pro purchase and charges the Apple Account; TextWiz never sees card data. Subscription entitlement state is cached locally on the Mac. No account, no login, no licensing server.

## FAQ

### Where is the latest TextWiz release available?
TextWiz 1.6.0 (19), released on October 9, 2026, is available on GitHub. The Mac App Store update is not yet available. See the changelog for the release notes and GitHub link.

### How much does TextWiz cost?
TextWiz is a free download on the Mac App Store. The Demo provider is free forever. TextWiz Pro unlocks every real AI provider: $2.99 per week ($0.99 for the first week), $7.99 per month, or $59.99 per year in US dollars. For eligible customers, $0.99 is charged up front for one week. It then renews at $2.99 per week until cancelled. Eligibility and the exact price are shown in the App Store before purchase. Monthly and yearly have no introductory offer. Prices vary by region because Apple equalizes them per storefront.

### What is free and what needs TextWiz Pro?
The download is free and stays free, and the built-in Demo provider runs free and ungated forever so you can see exactly how the app behaves. Every run against a real provider needs TextWiz Pro: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Apple Intelligence, LM Studio, MLX-LM, Mistral, Groq, and OpenRouter all sit behind it, local engines included.

### Can I try TextWiz before subscribing?
Yes. Download the app and run the Demo provider, which is free, ungated, and permanent. It is the real interface with real wizards, so nothing about the flow is hidden from you. There is no trial period on any paid plan, because the free Demo provider does that job without a clock running. For eligible customers, the weekly plan starts at $0.99 for the first week. Eligibility and the exact price are shown in the App Store before purchase.

### How do I cancel TextWiz Pro?
Open System Settings > Apple Account > Media & Purchases > Subscriptions, pick TextWiz, and cancel. Cancel at least 24 hours before the current period ends, otherwise the next period is charged. Pro stays active until the end of the period you already paid for. Apple handles billing, so refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com.

### I already bought TextWiz. What happens to me?
You keep TextWiz Pro for life at no cost. Anyone who bought the paid app before the switch to free keeps full Pro access with nothing to buy and nothing to renew. Sign in with the same Apple Account you bought it with and TextWiz restores your access.

### How do I use TextWiz?
Two flows. Copy text with ⌘C and press ⌘⇧Space — the floating panel opens with your clipboard as input and runs the wizard you pick. Or right-click the selection → Services → Process with TextWiz, and macOS replaces it in place. Choose any built-in wizard — Proofread, Rewrite, Concise, Friendly, Professional, X Post, LinkedIn Post, and more — or run one you built yourself.

### Which AI providers does TextWiz support?
Ten engines out of the box, four of them on-device: Apple Intelligence (Apple Foundation Model—no API key on supported Macs, requires TextWiz Pro), Ollama, LM Studio, and MLX-LM. Cloud: Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Mistral, Groq, and OpenRouter. Every real provider requires TextWiz Pro except the Demo provider. Choose one Primary Provider and Model in Settings—all wizards use that pair unless you override in a custom wizard.

### Do I need an API key?
Cloud providers need your own API key—stored in the macOS Keychain and only sent to the provider you chose. On-device engines (Apple Intelligence, Ollama, LM Studio, and MLX-LM) need no API key, but TextWiz Pro is still required for every real provider except the Demo provider.

### Can I add a cloud model of my own?
Yes. Each built-in cloud provider offers three suggested defaults plus your added API model IDs. In Dashboard → Providers, enter the exact API model ID, including its namespace where required, then use Validate & Add. TextWiz checks that specific model before saving without generating text; a valid API key alone is not enough. Older catalog models remain available to saved wizards and can be added explicitly. Local engines list the installed models they discover.

### Can I use a custom OpenAI-compatible provider?
Yes. Open Dashboard → Providers → Add Custom Provider and enter an absolute HTTPS base URL with a host and any API prefix, such as https://api.example.com/v1. Embedded credentials, query parameters, and fragments are rejected. Existing custom HTTP endpoints must be edited to HTTPS before use; built-in local engines keep their HTTP setup. Enter model API IDs one per line and put credentials in the API Key field, which stores them in macOS Keychain. Additional headers are plaintext routing metadata and should not contain secrets.

### What are wizards and collections?
A wizard (or "wiz") is one AI spell—a named prompt that transforms the text you select. TextWiz ships 14 built-in wizards: 13 visible actions in Everyday Edits (Proofread, Rewrite, Concise, Friendly, Professional), Social (X Post, LinkedIn Post), and Analyst & Coach (Clarity Critic, Executive Summary, Decision Extractor, Rewrite Coach, Argument Stress Test, Structure Tightener), plus Improve Prompt in the wizard editor. You can also build unlimited wizards of your own—write the prompt, pick the provider and model, and it shows up in the panel alongside the built-ins.

### Can TextWiz write the result back into my document?
Yes — two ways. Via right-click → Services → Process with TextWiz, macOS replaces the selection after a successful, complete result. On failure, refusal, or an incomplete result, your selected text stays intact and the floating panel opens. Via the ⌘⇧Space hotkey, click Copy to put the result on the clipboard, close the panel, and return focus to your previous app, then press ⌘V. Auto-copy is a Settings option and is off by default. If the panel was opened from TextWiz itself, Copy just closes it. No Accessibility permission is needed.

### Does TextWiz keep a history of my requests?
Yes. Every run is saved locally so you can browse, search, and reopen past results from the History view. It's stored in SQLite on your Mac—never uploaded anywhere.

### What is the diff view?
Inline highlighting of what changed between your original text and the AI result—word and character-level, additions in green and deletions in red. Enabled by default in the floating panel.

### Where does my data go? Is it private?
TextWiz runs no servers and collects none of your data. With on-device providers (Apple Intelligence, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX-LM), nothing ever leaves your Mac. With cloud providers, only the text you process is sent—directly to the provider you chose, never to us. History and analytics live in local SQLite; API keys stay in the macOS Keychain.

### What does TextWiz offer for writing in other Mac apps?
TextWiz opens a floating AI panel from your clipboard with ⌘⇧Space, or processes selected text through the macOS Services menu. It needs no Accessibility permission. Choose an on-device engine to keep text on your Mac without per-token costs, or bring your own cloud API key; cloud usage is billed by the provider. Every real provider, including on-device engines, requires TextWiz Pro. The Demo provider is free forever.

### Does TextWiz need the Accessibility permission?
No. TextWiz captures text through two fully compliant paths: the system clipboard (you press ⌘C, then ⌘⇧Space) and the macOS Services menu (right-click → Services → Process with TextWiz). It does not call any Accessibility APIs. You won't see any permission prompts on first launch — it just works, even in Slack, VS Code, and other sandboxed apps.
